class.name: VoxelMesherDualContouring
class.brief_description: Builds smooth voxel meshes that keep sharp edges and corners.
class.description: Dual contouring mesher for [VoxelTerrain]. It places one vertex per cell where the tangent planes of the surface crossings in that cell meet. Sharp edges and corners need the exact surface normal at each crossing, which a voxel grid doesn't hold: within about a voxel of a feature, any normal estimated from stored SDF values blends the faces meeting there. A generator that knows its shapes (a room carved into terrain, a wall) can write exact normals into the channels named by [member edge_normals_channel], and those features then come out sharp. Elsewhere the mesher uses the SDF's gradient, and features round off much like with [VoxelMesherTransvoxel]. Vertex attributes match [VoxelMesherTransvoxel]: [code]CUSTOM0[/code] holds LOD data (always zero, since this mesher has no LOD transitions) and [code]CUSTOM1[/code] holds texture data in the Single layout, so materials written for Transvoxel work unchanged. It does not support [VoxelLodTerrain]. It needs 2 voxels of padding on each side of a block.

members.member: First of 3 consecutive channels, each 32-bit, holding exact surface data for the voxel edges along X, Y and Z. Each edge is stored on its lower voxel: bits 0-7 are where the surface crosses it, as a fraction of the edge from 1 to 255 (0 means no data), and bits 8-19 and 20-31 are the outward normal (toward air) in octahedral encoding, each axis mapped from -1..1 to 0..4095. Stored data is only used while the crossing it describes is still within a quarter of an edge of where the SDF puts it now, so voxels edited after generation fall back to the gradient. -1 disables it.
How much each vertex is pulled toward the average of the surface crossings in its cell. Higher values tidy flat areas but soften features.

Directions of the error function weaker than this fraction of the strongest are ignored when placing a vertex. Lower values keep more features but can place vertices badly where planes are nearly parallel.
How material indices are encoded in vertices. See [enum TexturingMode].

constants.constant: Each voxel has one 8-bit material index in [constant VoxelBuffer.CHANNEL_INDICES]; up to 4 blend per cell, encoded like [constant VoxelMesherTransvoxel.TEXTURES_SINGLE_S4].
